title: Straightening of left and right fibrations restricts space-valued transport
statement: Use quasicategories, Kan complexes, coherent functors, functor simplicial sets, cores and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], left, right, Cartesian and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], space-valued transport of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], cocartesian straightening of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], the infinity category of small quasicategories of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure] and the opposite involution of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-opposite-involution]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ and let $B$ be a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory. Let $i:\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$ regard a $\mathcal U$-small Kan complex as a quasicategory; for Kan complexes $K,L$ the simplicial set $\operatorname{Fun}(K,L)$ is Kan and equal to its core, so $i$ is a coherent fully faithful functor. (1) Every left fibration $p:E\to B$ is a cocartesian fibration, every edge of $E$ is $p$-cocartesian, and its fibers are Kan complexes. Hence every functor over $B$ between left fibrations preserves cocartesian edges, and the left fibrations with $\mathcal U$-small total space span a full subcategory $\operatorname{LFib}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{coCart}(B)$ whose mapping spaces are the Kan complexes $\operatorname{Fun}_{/B}(E,E')$. (2) Write $T_B:\operatorname{LFib}(B)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ for space-valued transport and $\operatorname{St}_B$ for cocartesian straightening. There is a coherent natural equivalence $\operatorname{St}_B|_{\operatorname{LFib}(B)}\simeq i\circ T_B$ of functors $\operatorname{LFib}(B)\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U})$, whose component at $p$ evaluated at $b$ is equivalent to the identity of the fiber $E_b$. In particular a left fibration classified by $F:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ under space-valued transport is classified by $i\circ F$ as a cocartesian fibration. (3) Dually every right fibration $q:Y\to B$ is a Cartesian fibration all of whose edges are $q$-Cartesian. Define the Cartesian straightening of a Cartesian fibration $E\to B$ as $\mathrm{op}\circ\operatorname{St}_{B^{\mathrm{op}}}(E^{\mathrm{op}}\to B^{\mathrm{op}}):B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$. Then a right fibration classified by $X:B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ under the right-fibration form of space-valued transport is classified by $i\circ X$ under Cartesian straightening, and the right fibrations form a full subcategory of the Cartesian fibrations on which this identification is a coherent natural equivalence. All these identifications are natural for maps of fibrations over $B$, including higher simplices, compatible with base change along maps $B'\to B$, and unchanged on enlarging $\mathcal U'$.

source.place: HTT Proposition 2.4.2.4 (left fibrations are the cocartesian fibrations with Kan fibers, every edge cocartesian) and Sections 2.2.1 and 3.2.1 (straightening of a left fibration agrees with the marked straightening of E^sharp); used implicitly in GHN Section 9 (the identification P(B) = RFib(B) inside Cart(B) before Proposition 9.7 and in the proof of Lemma 9.10(2)).

proof.text: First use the horn definitions, without invoking a characterization theorem as a black box. A left fibration lifts every inner horn, hence its total space over the quasicategory B is a quasicategory: fill the base inner horn in B and then lift that filler. It lifts every initial outer horn with any prescribed first edge, so every edge is cocartesian by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Lifting the horn with n=1 and i=0 supplies an edge over every base edge with prescribed source. Thus it is a cocartesian fibration. Reversing vertex order exchanges the initial and final horns, giving the Cartesian assertions for right fibrations. Apply the Kan-fiber clause of [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] to a right fibration (with F=E and q=p). For a left fibration apply it to its opposite and reverse the fiber back; reversal permutes all horn indices, so preserves the Kan condition. All these arguments allow empty fibers.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.2.4: the (1)-(2) horn calculation and the Kan-fiber assertion; dual for left fibrations.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], the mapping simplicial set between two left fibrations is the Kan complex Fun_{/B}(E,E'). Every map over B preserves cocartesian edges, since all target edges are cocartesian by step 1. The left fibrations therefore span a full subcategory of coCart(B); the right version is identical with Cartesian in place of cocartesian. Also Fun(K,L) is Kan for Kan complexes K,L: apply the mapping-complex clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] over the point. Every edge of a Kan complex is an equivalence by the converse outer-horn criterion of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling]. Consequently Fun(K,L) equals its core. The mapping-space model of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] and the coherent-nerve mapping comparison of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identify the inclusion of Kan complexes with the coherent fully faithful functor i in the statement.

source.place: Sections 2.2.1 and 3.1.4: mapping complexes, Cat infinity and the full subcategory of spaces.

proof.text: Compute the Cartesian comparison first, in the cone presentations of the two straightening equivalences. For a small quasicategory A choose the object-preserving locally Kan replacement I=R C[A] and its Dwyer--Kan equivalence u:C[A] -> I from [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Put C=I^op and phi=u:C[A] -> C^op. The unmarked cone adjunction L_phi dashv U_phi of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen] is a Quillen equivalence from the contravariant slice to Kan-model C-diagrams. The marked cone adjunction St^+_phi dashv Un^+_phi of [lem-coef-marked-cone-straightening-quillen] is a Quillen equivalence from the Cartesian marked slice to marked C-diagrams. The identity of underlying cone formulas is literal: both use D_X=C^op amalg_{C[X]} C[X star Delta^0] and the value D_X(c,*). The marked construction adds the specified edges to this same simplicial set, and changes no underlying simplices.

proof.text:
Let F:C -> sSet be objectwise Kan, and mark every edge in each value, giving F^sharp. For any marked X over A, adjunction and step 3 give natural bijections
Hom_+(X,Un^+_phi(F^sharp)) = Nat_+(St^+_phi X,F^sharp) = Nat(L_phi(underlying X),F) = Hom_{/A}(underlying X,U_phi F).
The middle equality holds because every target edge is marked; the enriched action is the same cone action. The final set also equals Hom_+(X,(U_phi F)^sharp). Naturality in all X identifies Un^+_phi(F^sharp) with (U_phi F)^sharp, over A, including its markings. Naturality in F follows from postcomposition in these bijections. Apply the same calculation to X times (Delta^n)^sharp: both sides then consist of exactly the same maps on underlying simplices. Thus this comparison respects transformations and every simplex operator, rather than just comparing values at base vertices.

source.place: Definition 3.2.1.2 and the right-adjoint construction: the all-marked-target adjunction calculation.

proof.text: Pass the comparison of step 4 to infinity localizations using [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. An objectwise Kan F and F^sharp are projectively fibrant in the two diagram models. Both right adjoints preserve weak equivalences between fibrant diagrams, by [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], so their derived values are the values in step 4. The unmarked output is a right fibration by [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen], whose every edge is Cartesian by step 1; its natural marking is therefore precisely sharp. Rectification [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification] identifies the two diagram localizations with Fun(A^op,S) and Fun(A^op,Cat_infinity), and sharp with postcomposition by i. Its hypotheses hold: the Kan model is combinatorial and simplicial by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] at the terminal category, and the marked model is so by [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]; the projective structures and the Dwyer--Kan index change are supplied by the two cone nodes and the reversal C[A^op]=C[A]^op in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. The universal property of localization retains the comparison as a coherent natural equivalence. Composing with the inverse straightening equivalences gives Cartesian straightening of a right fibration classified by X equal to i composed with X, on the whole right-fibration category.

source.place: Theorems 2.2.1.2 and 3.2.0.1 with Proposition 4.2.4.4: derive the actual adjunction comparison, not merely an equivalence of homotopy categories.

proof.text: Spell out the harmless opposite on space values needed for the cocartesian convention. There is a natural homeomorphism r_K:|K^op| -> |K|, [sigma;(t_0,...,t_n)] maps to [sigma;(t_n,...,t_0)]. The quotient formula of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] shows this is well-defined: reversal changes alpha:[m] -> [n] to alpha^vee(j)=n-alpha(m-j), exactly the opposite operator; reversing twice is the identity. The natural zigzag K^op -> Sing(|K^op|) -> Sing(|K|) <- K uses r_K in the middle and the realization-singular units on either end. Those units are weak homotopy equivalences by [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak]. Localizing it in the Kan model therefore identifies the opposite-space functor O with the identity, coherently in K, by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Here O is the restriction of the coherent opposite involution to spaces: it has the same ordinary maps K -> L sent to K^op -> L^op, and localization's functor-category universal property identifies their extensions. In particular op composed with i is naturally equivalent to i, with fiberwise component the usual identification of a space with its opposite. This uses no degreewise identity Fun(K,L)=Fun(K^op,L^op).

source.place: Section 1.2.1 (opposites); direct reversal of realization coordinates, followed by the cited realization-singular and localization results.

proof.text: For a left fibration p over B, its opposite is a right fibration over B^op. Apply step 5 to that fibration. Take the coherent opposite of its classified categories and use step 6 on the space-valued diagram. By the opposite definition of cocartesian straightening, this yields St_B(p) equivalent to i composed with T_B(p). This also follows directly at the ordinary right-adjoint level: the covariant unstraightening is (U_{B^op}F)^op by [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]; step 4 gives the identical formula for the marked right adjoint, and step 6 removes the opposite on its Kan values. Thus the comparison uses the specified space-valued transport, including its higher simplices, not an arbitrarily chosen functor with the same vertex values. Evaluate at b and use the two fiber identifications of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] and [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]: the comparison identifies the same fiber E_b with itself. The double coordinate reversal is the identity, so the component is equivalent to that identity. Taking opposites once more and using op squared equivalent to the identity recovers exactly the Cartesian straightening op composed with St_{B^op}(q^op) stated for right fibrations.

source.place: Sections 1.2.1, 2.2.1 and 3.2.1: the covariant dual, with both opposite operations retained.

proof.text: The cone formulas and the adjunction bijections in step 4 commute with restriction of a base simplex. The base-change isomorphisms of [lem-coef-marked-cone-straightening-quillen] agree for composites and identities; the unmarked comparison has the same substitution, as the base-change clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] states. After rectification this is precisely the pullback/precomposition comparison in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] and [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Since the comparison came from the same natural adjunction bijections before localization, its localization is compatible with these isomorphisms on transformations and all higher simplices. The coordinate reversal in step 6 is also natural and independent of the base. All constructions use small cone simplicial sets, small Kan-valued diagrams, and replacements in the input universe as in the marked-model and unmarked-presentation nodes. The small representative clause of space transport applies because B is U-small. Enlarging only U' changes neither these objects nor their mapping complexes or comparison maps; the opposite node explicitly has the same universe compatibility. This proves the remaining base-change and containing-universe assertions.
